items.text: The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.
The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
Docstring typo 'humam readible' in incident_occurrence.py:132 should be 'human readable'
The module incidents.py declares `import logging` / `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` but never uses `logger` - no `logger.` call exists in the file
Require at least `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins before opening the incident.

get_monitor_environment_context() creates a local config copy and modifies schedule_type to a human-readable display value, but line 168 returns monitor_environment.monitor.config (the original) instead of the local config variable, silently discarding the transformation. Line 168 should use 'config' instead of 'monitor_environment.monitor.config'

get_monitor_environment_context builds a copy of monitor config with schedule_type replaced by display name, but returns the raw monitor.config instead of the modified copy, so human-readable schedule_type never reaches the event context (incident_occurrence.py:160 creates config copy but line 168 returns original)

If `failed_checkins` contains only statuses not in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`, `status_counts` will be empty and this can yield a user-visible message like `" check-ins detected"` despite the docstring mentioning a generic fallback. Consider explicitly handling the empty-count case to avoid confusing evidence text.
The module incident_occurrence.py declares `import logging` / `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` but never uses `logger` - no `logger.` call exists in the file

The `failed_checkin: MonitorCheckIn` parameter forces the caller to re-query `MonitorCheckIn` objects from the database even though `previous_checkins` already contains the relevant check-in data and `monitor_environment` is already known at the call site. Consider passing `monitor_environment` and `trace_id` directly instead of requiring a full model fetch.

In `get_monitor_environment_context`, the function copies `monitor.config` and replaces `schedule_type` with its display name, but then returns the raw `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead, so the readable schedule type never reaches the event context
Typo in comment: 'commits' should be 'check-ins' on line 51

get_monitor_environment_context() copies and mutates config["schedule_type"] to a display value but returns monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the modified config variable, so the transformation is never applied to the occurrence context payload
Typo in docstring: 'humam' should be 'human' on line 132

`config` is copied and `schedule_type` is converted to a display value, but the returned payload uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so this transformation is currently ignored. If the intent was to publish a human-readable `schedule_type`, it won't happen as written.
Non-idiomatic iteration: should use next(iter(status_counts.keys())) instead of list(status_counts.keys())[0] on line 146

Bug: `config` is copied and updated with the human-readable `schedule_type`, but the return dict references `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original) instead of the local `config`. The `schedule_type` transformation is lost.

If there are fewer than `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins available, `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` will still return a shorter list and the code proceeds to open an incident. This seems at odds with the "N consecutive missed or failed check-ins in a row" threshold semantics (it could create an incident on the first failure for a brand-new monitor).
Unused logger variable defined in both new modules (incidents.py:11, incident_occurrence.py:25) - grep finds no logger. calls in these files or mark_failed.py
Bug: Modified config copy is not used in return value - line 168 returns original monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the modified config copy

Patch removes public names from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, SimpleCheckIn, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context) which could break downstream imports or mock.patch strings in external code

issues.claim: get_monitor_environment_context() in incident_occurrence.py copies the monitor config and replaces schedule_type with its human-readable display value, but returns monitor_environment.monitor.config (the original, line 168) instead of the modified copy. The schedule_type transformation therefore never reaches the event context.

The code re-fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID from the database to pass as the failed_checkin parameter, even though previous_checkins already holds the needed data and monitor_environment is known at the call site. This is an unnecessary database query.
The docstring at incident_occurrence.py line 132 contains the typo 'humam readible' instead of 'human readable'.
incidents.py defines `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` but never uses it.
incident_occurrence.py defines `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` but never uses it.

When fewer than failure_issue_threshold check-ins exist, previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold] returns a shorter list and the code still opens an incident. This contradicts the N-consecutive-failures threshold semantics; for example, a new monitor can get an incident on its first failure.

If failed_checkins contains only statuses not in HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, status_counts is empty and the evidence message becomes " check-ins detected". There is no generic fallback, although the docstring mentions one.
The comment on line 51 says 'commits' where it should say 'check-ins'.
Line 146 uses list(status_counts.keys())[0] instead of next(iter(status_counts.keys())).

The patch removes public names from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed: mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, SimpleCheckIn, get_failure_reason and get_monitor_environment_context. Downstream imports or mock.patch targets that reference them will break.
